authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: The company completed the acquisition of The Bellmoor Inn & Spa, a 79-room hotel in Rehoboth Beach, Delaware, for $31.0 million. It was funded with cash on hand.
In its third quarter 2026 earnings release, the company raised its full-year 2026 guidance. It cited stronger third quarter results and an improved fourth quarter booking pace.
The company increased its quarterly common dividend by 22% to $0.11 per share.
no_value_reason: no valuation route yet for a real estate company or trust

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description.
business_model.claim: DiamondRock is a lodging REIT that owns premium hotels and resorts. It owns the hotels but does not operate them, and it keeps the hotels' operating profit or loss after paying manager and brand fees. At year-end 2025 it owned 35 hotels with 9,595 rooms in 26 U.S. markets.
quotes: We are an owner, as opposed to an operator, of the hotels in our portfolio.
As of December 31, 2025, we owned 35 hotels with 9,595 rooms located in 26 markets in the United States.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and in the 8-K about the acquisition. The 35-hotel count in the release is consistent with the post-acquisition portfolio, but the evidence does not say so directly.
business_model.claim: The portfolio changed during 2026. At September 30, 2026 the company owned 34 hotels with 9,400 rooms. It then bought a further hotel on October 1, 2026 for $31.0 million, funded with cash on hand. The earnings release describes a portfolio of 35 hotels.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we owned a portfolio of 34 premium hotels and resorts that contain 9,400 guest rooms located in 26 different markets in the United States.
The acquisition was funded with cash on hand

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q income statement and MD&A. 'Other' revenue is described in the 10-K as primarily spa, parking, resort fees and attrition and cancellation fees.
business_model.claim: The company sells hotel stays and related services. Revenue is reported as rooms, food and beverage, and other. For the nine months to September 30, 2026 (table in thousands), total revenues were 874,053, split into rooms 567,205, food and beverage 220,115 and other 86,733. Rooms are about 65% of revenue.
quotes: Room revenue comprised approximately 65% of our total revenues for the nine months ended September 30, 2026

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K business and risk sections and the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Customers are business and leisure travelers and groups staying at luxury and upper-upscale hotels in major urban markets and resort destinations. Demand depends on business travel, tourism and the economy. Management said the third quarter of 2026 had healthy demand and higher rates in both transient and group segments.
quotes: Our hotels and resorts are primarily categorized as luxury and upper upscale as defined by STR, Inc.
dependence on business travelers and tourism, both of which vary with consumer and business confidence in the strength of the economy;
healthy demand and higher rates across both transient and group segments

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K business and risk sections. The fee amounts are from the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: All hotels are run by third-party managers, who earn fees based on hotel revenues and profitability. Brand owners such as Marriott, Hilton and IHG receive franchise fees where a hotel is franchised. Nine-month 2026 management fees were 21,798 and franchise fees were 29,936 (table in thousands). Of 35 hotels, 18 were under franchise agreements.
quotes: All of our hotels are managed by a third party, either an independent operator or a brand operator, such as Marriott.
As of the date of this report, 18 of our 35 hotels operate under Marriott, Hilton, or IHG franchise agreements.

business_model.basis: Metric definitions are stated in the 10-Q MD&A. The figures are in the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Hotel revenue is driven by occupancy, ADR and RevPAR. In the third quarter of 2026, comparable occupancy was 77.8% versus 75.8% a year earlier and comparable ADR was $290.46 versus $279.91. Comparable RevPAR rose 6.6%.
quotes: RevPAR, which is calculated as the product of ADR and occupancy percentage

business_model.basis: Cost categories are described in the 10-Q MD&A. Amounts are from the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Costs are mostly hotel-level. They are rooms, food and beverage, other departmental and support expenses, management fees, franchise fees and other property-level expenses. Other property-level expenses cover property taxes, insurance, ground lease expense and other fixed costs. For the nine months to September 30, 2026 (table in thousands), rooms expense was 135,826, food and beverage 145,724, other departmental and support 207,310 and other property-level 65,268.
quotes: Other property-level expenses include property taxes, insurance, ground lease expense, and other fixed costs.

business_model.basis: Figures are stated in the earnings release. The mechanism is stated in the 10-K risk factors.
business_model.claim: Fixed costs create operating leverage. In the third quarter of 2026, comparable hotel operating expenses rose 3.9% while comparable total revenues rose 6.4%. Comparable Hotel Adjusted EBITDA margin was 30.81%, up from 29.15%.
quotes: In periods of weak demand, profitability is negatively affected by the relatively high fixed costs of operating premium full-service hotels as compared to other classes of hotels.

business_model.basis: Balance and expense figures are from the 10-Q statements. The debt composition is from the 10-K. The reason for the 2026 decline is not stated in the evidence.
business_model.claim: Financing cost is a smaller expense line. Debt, net of issuance costs, was 1,099,131 at September 30, 2026 (table in thousands). Interest expense was 14,648 in the third quarter versus 17,111 a year earlier. The debt is unsecured term loans, with no borrowings on the revolving credit facility at the end of 2025.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, our outstanding debt consists of unsecured term loans, and we had no outstanding borrowings under our senior unsecured credit facility.

business_model.basis: Strategy is stated in the 10-K. Amounts are from the 10-Q statements and the 8-K.
business_model.claim: Capital recycling is a second source of value. The company sells non-core hotels and buys others. A hotel sale in the nine months to September 30, 2026 produced a net gain of 31,352 and net proceeds of 29,871 (tables in thousands). The company also bought a hotel for $31.0 million after quarter-end.
quotes: Separately, we regularly evaluate opportunities to dispose of non-core hotels.

business_model.basis: Cash flow figures are from the 10-Q. The distribution requirement is stated in the 10-K risk factors. The dividend increase is in the earnings release.
business_model.claim: Cash generation and payout follow REIT rules. Nine-month operating cash flow in 2026 was 174,255, against capital expenditures of 59,240 and common distributions of 62,241 (table in thousands). The company must distribute at least 90% of REIT taxable income, and it raised its quarterly dividend 22% to $0.11 per share.
quotes: because we generally must distribute at least 90% of our REIT taxable income each year to maintain our REIT tax status

competitive_position.claim: DRH is a self-managed lodging REIT that owns a portfolio of premium hotels and resorts: 34 hotels with 9,400 rooms in 26 U.S. markets at the latest quarter-end. It is an owner, not an operator, and all hotels are run by third-party managers.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, we owned a portfolio of 34 premium hotels and resorts that contain 9,400 guest rooms located in 26 different markets in the United States.

competitive_position.claim: Positioning: the 10-K describes the portfolio as luxury and upper upscale hotels in high barrier-to-entry markets. Nearly 40% of the portfolio is run as independent hotels and the rest carries Marriott, Hilton or IHG brands.
quotes: Our hotels and resorts are primarily categorized as luxury and upper upscale as defined by STR, Inc. and are generally located in high barrier-to-entry markets with multiple demand generators.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (management view, not independently tested)
competitive_position.claim: Management describes the portfolio as relatively insulated from competitive new supply and aimed at higher-income consumers, with pricing power expected to hold.
quotes: Our portfolio is relatively insulated from competitive new supply and the majority of our hotels are marketed to higher-income consumers.

competitive_position.claim: Third-quarter comparable operating results improved against the prior-year quarter. Comparable RevPAR was $226.01, up 6.6%, and the comparable Hotel Adjusted EBITDA margin was 30.81%, up 166 basis points.
quotes: Comparable RevPAR: $226.01, an increase of 6.6% compared to the third quarter of 2025.
Comparable Hotel Adjusted EBITDA Margin: 30.81%, an increase of 166 basis points compared to the third quarter of 2025.

competitive_position.basis: figures stated in the release table; the cause is the company's own explanation
competitive_position.claim: Over nine months, comparable total revenues grew 4.9% while comparable hotel operating expenses grew only 1.0%, and comparable Hotel Adjusted EBITDA grew 14.6%. Management attributes this to owner-manager alignment and portfolio design, and calls it expense discipline.
quotes: Owner-manager alignment and portfolio design drive superior expense discipline

competitive_position.basis: inferred from the income statement line 'Loss (gain) on sale of hotel property, net'
competitive_position.claim: Nine-month net income attributable to common stockholders of 138,265 (table in thousands) includes a gain on hotel sale of 31,352 (table in thousands). Reported earnings therefore overstate the operating comparison with the prior year.

Balance-sheet strength supports its ability to invest: debt net of issuance costs was 1,099,131 (table in thousands) against cash of 139,963 (table in thousands), and all hotels were unencumbered by mortgage debt at the prior year-end. It funded a $31.0 million acquisition of The Bellmoor Inn & Spa from cash on hand.
quotes: We maintain balance sheet flexibility with our existing corporate cash, capacity under our senior unsecured credit facility and all of our hotels unencumbered by mortgage debt as of December 31, 2025.

The acquisition was funded with cash on hand and represents an attractive opportunity to acquire an independent resort in a supply-constrained market with strong in-place cash flow and meaningful operational upside.

competitive_position.claim: The company raised its quarterly common dividend by 22% to $0.11 per share and raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $322.0 to $327.0 (release table, in millions) from $310.0 to $320.0.
quotes: Common Dividend: The Company increased its quarterly common dividend by 22% to $0.11 per share.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (prior-year comparable results)
competitive_position.claim: EBITDA is geographically concentrated: Boston supplied 12.9%, Chicago 12.2% and New York City 7.1% of market EBITDA on the company's comparable basis. A downturn in a few urban markets would therefore weigh on results.
quotes: Boston 12.9% Chicago 12.2% New York City 7.1%

competitive_position.claim: Hotels in major metropolitan markets that may be targets of terrorism or other catastrophic events made up 71% of prior-year total revenues. Such events may be uninsurable or exceed policy limits.
quotes: These hotels constitute 71% of our total revenues in 2025.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (risk factor, no quantification)
competitive_position.claim: Threat: online travel intermediaries, AI-driven search and alternative lodging such as short-term rentals could pull bookings into costlier channels and press on rates and occupancy.
quotes: If bookings shift to higher cost distribution channels, including these internet travel intermediaries, it could materially impact our profitability.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: the premium full-service segment is cyclical and carries high fixed costs, so profitability suffers when demand is weak.
quotes: In periods of weak demand, profitability is negatively affected by the relatively high fixed costs of operating premium full-service hotels as compared to other classes of hotels.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: operating costs. The 10-K attributes a $13.3 million rise in hotel costs to property taxes (mainly at Chicago hotels), utilities and repairs, and expects labor, utilities and property taxes to keep pressuring margins.
quotes: The remaining increase of $13.3 million was due to higher property tax assessments, primarily related to our Chicago hotels, as well as increases in utilities and repairs and maintenance costs.

competitive_position.claim: Threat: dependence on third-party managers. The company cannot operate its hotels, and it may lack the rights to force a manager to change operations even if it considers a hotel run inefficiently.
quotes: Our results of operations are highly dependent on the management of our hotel properties by third-party hotel management companies.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (risk factor, no quantification)
competitive_position.claim: Threat: video conferencing and hybrid work can reduce business travel and hotel room demand.
quotes: The increased use of video conferencing technology by businesses has resulted in decreased business travel as companies have leveraged the use of technologies that allow multiple parties from different locations to participate in virtual meetings without traveling to a centralized meeting location, such as our hotels.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet and cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Cash and cash equivalents were 139,963 (table in thousands) at the latest balance sheet date, up from 68,084 (table in thousands) at the prior year-end. Restricted cash was 40,465 (table in thousands), shown separately.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 8-K; the link to the quarter-end cash balance is inferred.
financial_health.claim: After quarter-end the company paid $31.0 million in cash for The Bellmoor Inn & Spa. This reduces the cash balance reported at the quarter-end.
quotes: The acquisition was funded with cash on hand

financial_health.claim: The latest evidence on the revolver is year-end: $400.0 million of borrowing capacity and no outstanding borrowings. No later revolver availability figure is in the evidence.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we had $400.0 million of borrowing capacity under the Revolving Credit Facility.

financial_health.basis: Stated on the balance sheet and cash flow statement; the unchanged debt is read directly from them.
financial_health.claim: Debt, net of issuance costs, was 1,099,131 (table in thousands), essentially unchanged from 1,098,850 (table in thousands) at the prior year-end. Against it, total liabilities were 1,548,400 (table in thousands), total equity 1,548,452 (table in thousands) and total assets 3,096,852 (table in thousands).

At the prior year-end the debt was $1.1 billion with a weighted average interest rate of 4.98% (swaps included) and about 3.6 years of weighted average maturity if all extensions are used. The portfolio was fully free of secured debt.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we had $1.1 billion of debt outstanding with a weighted average interest rate of 4.98%, which includes the effect of interest rate swaps, and a weighted average maturity date of approximately 3.6 years, assuming all extension options available in our debt agreements are exercised.
As of December 31, 2025, our portfolio is fully unencumbered by secured debt.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the income statement and cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: Interest expense fell to 43,780 (table in thousands) for the nine months from 47,137 (table in thousands), and to 14,648 (table in thousands) for the quarter from 17,111 (table in thousands). Cash paid for interest was 41,945 (table in thousands) against 43,972 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement; no free cash flow figure is computed.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the income statement, cash flow statement and earnings release; the quality reading is inferred from these lines.

Sale proceeds of 29,871 (table in thousands) sit in investing. Due to/from hotel managers was an outflow of 23,708 (table in thousands).

financial_health.basis: Stated in the earnings release table.
financial_health.claim: Operating metrics improved in the quarter. Comparable hotel adjusted EBITDA margin was 30.81% against 29.15%, and nine-month adjusted FFO per diluted share was $0.98 against $0.82.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement and earnings release; the effect on later cash is inferred.

Repurchases were 1,856 (table in thousands), against 35,519 (table in thousands). The company also raised its quarterly common dividend by 22% to $0.11 per share.
quotes: The Company increased its quarterly common dividend by 22% to $0.11 per share.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A; the $500.0 million is the Term 1 Loan principal, and the link to the schedule is inferred.
financial_health.claim: As of the prior year-end, the maturity schedule showed no principal due before 2029. It then showed 500,000 (table in thousands) in 2029 and 600,000 (table in thousands) in 2030, assuming all extension options are exercised.
quotes: The maturity date of the Revolving Credit Facility, Term 1 Loan and Term 3 Loan may be extended for two additional six-month periods upon the payment of applicable fees and satisfaction of certain standard conditions.

financial_health.basis: Maturities are stated in the 10-K; how they will be met is inferred from the listed funding sources.
financial_health.claim: The Term 1 Loan of $500.0 million matures in 2028 before extension, the $300.0 million Term 3 Loan in 2029, and the $300.0 million Term 2 Loan in 2030, on top of the $400.0 million revolver. The evidence states no refinancing plan.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the Q3 release and 10-Q MD&A; the conditions are inferred from the 10-K risk language and the 2025 comparison (P3, P2).
growth_thesis.claim: Rate and occupancy gains lifted comparable RevPAR 6.6% to $226.01 in Q3 2026, from ADR up 3.8% and occupancy of 77.8% against 75.8% a year earlier. For this to continue, travel demand and pricing power must hold.
quotes: Comparable RevPAR: $226.01, an increase of 6.6% compared to the third quarter of 2025.
Travel demand remained strong through the first nine months of 2026, contributing to growth in occupancy, ADR and hotel revenues across many of our markets.

growth_thesis.basis: Margin and expense figures are stated in the release table; the continuation condition is inferred from the 10-K outlook.
growth_thesis.claim: Margin expansion is a second driver. Q3 comparable Hotel Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 166 basis points to 30.81%. Over nine months, comparable hotel operating expenses grew 1.0% against comparable total revenues up 4.9%. For this to continue, cost growth must stay below revenue growth.
quotes: Combined with the operating efficiencies we have built across the portfolio, that drove outsized Hotel Adjusted EBITDA growth and, importantly, higher free cash flow.
Comparable Hotel Adjusted EBITDA Margin: 30.81%, an increase of 166 basis points compared to the third quarter of 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Interest and preferred figures are stated in the 10-Q income statement; the mechanism is stated in the 10-K MD&A for 2025 and the preferred redemption.
growth_thesis.claim: Lower financing cost adds to earnings. Q3 interest expense fell to 14,648 (table in thousands) from 17,111, and nine-month interest expense fell to 43,780 from 47,137. Preferred distributions are now zero, against 2,454 in Q3 2025. For this to continue, debt must stay unsecured and the 2025 refinancing must hold.
quotes: The decrease in interest expense is primarily due to our mortgage debt repayments in 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Inferred from the income statement and cash flow adjustment lines.
growth_thesis.claim: Reported nine-month earnings growth overstates the operating trend. Nine-month net income attributable to common stockholders was 138,265 (table in thousands), against 67,855, and includes a gain on sale of hotel property of 31,352. For earnings growth to continue, it has to come from operations rather than disposal gains.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release guidance table and text.
growth_thesis.claim: Management guides to continued growth: it raised 2026 Adjusted FFO per diluted share guidance to $1.24 to $1.26 from $1.18 to $1.23. This rests on Q3 results and the Q4 booking pace, and assumes no further acquisitions, dispositions or repurchases. For it to be met, Q4 bookings must convert to revenue and costs must stay in line.
quotes: Given the strength of our third quarter results and our fourth quarter booking pace, we are raising our 2026 guidance again.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated by management in the release; the size of the effect is not quantified in the evidence.
growth_thesis.claim: Management points to recently renovated hotels ramping up as a 2027 earnings driver. For this to hold, the renovated hotels must reach their expected returns and renovation disruption must stay limited.
quotes: We expect to grow earnings through continued operating execution and the ramp of our recently renovated hotels

growth_thesis.basis: Dividend and cash flow figures are stated; the capital intensity target is a management claim in an investor presentation.
growth_thesis.claim: Free cash flow supports a higher dividend. The quarterly common dividend rose 22% to $0.11 per share. Nine-month operating cash flow was 174,255 (table in thousands) against capital expenditures of 59,240. Management plans capital spending of 7-9% of revenue annually over the medium term, against a peer average of 10%. For this to continue, operating cash flow must hold up and reinvestment must stay at the lower rate.
quotes: Common Dividend: The Company increased its quarterly common dividend by 22% to $0.11 per share.
Investing 7-9% of revenue annually over the medium term vs. a peer average of 10% over the last three years

growth_thesis.basis: Price, yield and funding are stated in the 8-K; the capacity condition is inferred from the balance sheet.

DRH bought The Bellmoor Inn & Spa for $31.0 million on October 1, 2026, funded with cash on hand, at a projected stabilized NOI yield of about 9.5%. For acquisitions to keep adding growth, cash and balance-sheet capacity must stay available.
quotes: The acquisition is not expected to have a material impact on the Company’s fourth quarter 2026 earnings.

growth_thesis.basis: Debt and asset figures are stated in the 10-Q balance sheet; the revolver capacity is a December 2025 figure from the 10-K, so current availability is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: A low-leverage balance sheet is the condition behind investment capacity. Debt was 1,099,131 (table in thousands) at September 30, 2026, essentially unchanged from 1,098,850, against total assets of 3,096,852. For growth to continue, access to the credit facility and capital markets must stay open.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we had $400.0 million of borrowing capacity under the Revolving Credit Facility.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-Q outlook; the link to this company's results is inferred from the risk language.

quotes: The outlook for the remainder of 2026 remains subject to economic, geopolitical and market uncertainty, including evolving conditions in the Middle East, persistent inflationary pressures, labor market conditions, elevated interest rates, increased borrowing costs, market volatility, and uncertainty regarding future monetary policy and capital market conditions.

risks.basis: Guidance table and management quote are stated; the risk of a miss is inferred.
